column1: # Fail-closed cases for example.readme-present. Tab-separated; `#` comments.
# Every row must FAIL the runtime with a non-zero exit and ZERO receipt bytes,
# and the stderr must contain the declared substring. The `cue` column records
# the `cue vet -d '#NormalizedCMIR'` verdict for the same file and the gate
# ASSERTS it, so the schema/runtime division of labour is measured rather than
# asserted in prose: `conforms` means CUE cannot see this fault and the runtime
# is the only thing standing between it and execution.
